original_question: Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold whose first Betti number is at least one. Is every even integral second cohomology class a ∈ H 2 (M ; R) of dual Thurston norm one realised as the Euler class of some tight contact structure on M ?
target_in_paper: Question 2.11 in §2.4 ('Euler classes of tight contact structures'), introduced as the contact version of Thurston's conjecture; not the nearby virtual taut-foliation Question 2.1 in §2.1. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official question almost verbatim: a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold M, the hypothesis b_1(M)≥1, an even integral second cohomology class a of dual Thurston norm one, and the conclusion asking whether a is realised as the Euler class of some tight contact structure on M. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, it should spell out that a is being viewed in real cohomology while carrying an integrality/parity condition; the paper phrases this as 'an even integral second cohomology class a ∈ H^2(M; R)', leaving the precise meaning of 'even integral' implicit. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It should define 'dual Thurston norm one' explicitly as norm 1 with respect to the norm on H^2(M; R) dual to Thurston's norm on H_2(M; R); the paper uses the phrase without redefinition in Question 2.11. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It is slightly sharper to name the contact structure ξ and state the target equality as e(ξ)=a. The paper states the conclusion verbally as 'realised as the Euler class of some tight contact structure on M'. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

If one wants a fully explicit quantifier, state 'for every such a'; the paper's question is universally quantified over all even integral classes of dual Thurston norm one. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with first Betti number b_1(M)≥1. For every class a ∈ H^2(M; R) that is integral and even (that is, a lies in the image of H^2(M; Z)→H^2(M; R) and is twice another integral class) and whose norm with respect to the norm on H^2(M; R) dual to Thurston's norm on H_2(M; R) is 1, does there exist a tight contact structure ξ on M with Euler class e(ξ)=a? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the exact official formulation Question 2.11 in §2.4, which the paper explicitly presents as the 'contact version of Thurston's conjecture.' The surrounding paragraph supplies the intended scope: Eliashberg's inequality gives the dual-Thurston-norm ≤ 1 constraint for Euler classes of tight contact structures, and taut foliations on irreducible 3-manifolds can be C^0-approximated by tight contact structures, which is exactly the motivation given for asking the Euler-class-one realization question. I therefore kept the scope on M itself and on tight contact structures, rather than drifting to the distinct virtual taut-foliation problem in Question 2.1. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
